description:
## Goal

Make derivation of one executable RuntimeDemand value a pure function of authoritative inputs, independent of which other demand formula happened to run or intern a type first. Reactive scheduling intentionally evaluates only changed formulas and cannot preserve a global member order.

## Proven defect

`settle_demand_cone` sorts members by StableSortKey because callable-flow derivation mints fresh Ty combinations as a side effect. HashMap iteration would otherwise change type interning order and downstream identities. That sorting barrier makes the present cone deterministic but cannot be a correctness requirement of the per-executable reactive model.

A four-process `00420_enum_take_drop_split` arena census produced equal arena lengths with 16 differing slots. The live clusters include address variables minted in different orders and equivalent callable unions constructed through different sequences. The interner assigns Ty ids from insertion order, so the differing arena proves an order-dependent construction sequence upstream.

Cross-process causal comparison shows the effect reaches product work: CallableConstruction cache-hit counts are the only excluded dimension in the permanent comparison, with pair agreement as low as 1 of 15 on one target fixture. Different intermediate type decompositions demand genuinely different construction-product sets. The defect is therefore observable in compilation work even when final programs remain canonical.

## Output contract

- Deriving one executable demand and callable-flow answer depends only on canonical authoritative facts and current demand inputs.
- Evaluating independent or cyclic formulas in several orders publishes semantically identical facts, identical demanded product identities, and byte-identical backend programs.
- No formula depends on a peer having minted a raw Ty or TypeVarId first.
- Determinism comes from canonical construction data, not sorting formula evaluation, translating unstable ids, or caching a schedule-dependent result.
- The reactive scheduler is free to evaluate only the formulas whose inputs moved.

## Strategy

1. Build a focused harness that evaluates the same independent and cyclic formulas in explicit shuffled orders.
2. Trace type creation through address-variable construction, `derive_callable_flow_facts_for_executable_product`, ground dispatch surfaces, callable boundary contributions, and own-surface demand.
3. Move type construction to the earliest authoritative fact, reuse an existing canonical type, or make the interning key structurally canonical.
4. Remove the global StableSortKey member-order dependency once shuffled evaluation is green.

The interner itself is not the target unless two structurally equal descriptions fail to deduplicate. That separate equivalence defect belongs to fz-kdt.48.

## TDD and acceptance

- Shuffled independent and cyclic formula evaluation yields identical demand/callable-flow facts and product request multisets.
- A multi-process arena-identity regression produces byte-identical arenas for this defect class.
- Delete the CallableConstruction cache-hit exclusion from `causal_work_multisets_agree_across_two_processes`; the test remains green.
- Raw scheduler order may differ without changing semantic values, demanded products, or output.
- No new sort, stable-id translation table, or demand-local cache is introduced.
- Persistent same-root no-op requests evaluate no demand formulas.

## Checks and documentation

Run focused shuffle tests, multi-process arena tests, backend determinism, target fixtures across interp/run/build, full library and single-threaded matrix, and clippy with warnings denied. Remove documentation claiming demand correctness requires a stable global member order and describe canonical formula inputs instead.
title: Make each RuntimeDemand formula order-independent before reactive scheduling
